facts: MID97 ADD_ENERGY is constructed in one function and the original request body is an empty table.
Successful response supplies buy_energy_times and updates selfPlayer.buyEnergyTimes.
Pass100 OTA patches only the request parameters; the response/event handling remains source-native.
Failed non-chat web requests are retained in pendingRequests with the same params table.
Retry invokes webRequest_ with the same MID and same params table, so an OTA-injected operation identity survives automatic retry unchanged.
xyd.generateUUID() exists in the effective source and returns a UUID-shaped random identifier.
Existing client systems already use xyd.generateUUID() for message/object identity, making it the source-native nonce primitive for the preservation bridge.

The purchase UI reads selfPlayer.buyEnergyTimes, prices ordinal buyEnergyTimes+1, checks VIP/Monthly allowance, and blocks initiating a new purchase when current Energy reaches the source energyMaxLimit.
Independent Energy UI path confirms the same 120-Energy purchase grant and purchase-count semantics.
buy_energy_cost is indexed by purchase ordinal.
Reachable ordinal costs through VIP15 plus Monthly Privilege are source-generated into energy_purchase_source_meta.json.
Active Monthly Privilege row 1 contributes num_energy=4 additional purchases; MID97 reads this entitlement but does not own its lifecycle.
energy_max_limit is 500; source UI treats it as a pre-purchase threshold, not a hard post-credit cap.
VIP num_energy supplies the base daily paid-Energy purchase allowance; existing VipPrivilegeResolver is the canonical backend reader.

bridge_contract.reason_for_uuid: A per-click UUID prevents operation-key reuse across daily ordinal resets or deliberate host-clock rollback while Backend.lua still preserves the same UUID for a network retry.
bridge_contract.unpatched_behavior: Empty/unidentified MID97 requests fail closed instead of risking an ambiguous charge.
